featured_reviews.review_text:
This famous temple located in Nirmal Village of Nalasopara which is situated at a hillock around two Nirmal lakes.
It is an old temple which has fort like stone structure with temples of Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu family. This temple has a Samadhi(shrine) of Shankaracharya.
In temple premises, there are also many small temples of Lord Shiva, Ganesha, Hanuman, Lord Ram, etc.
Every year there's a week long Fair which begins from Karthik Ekadashi. The special fair transforms the temple area into a venue of grand celebration which thousands of people comes to visit from nearby villages.

featured_reviews.name: Dhiraj Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Aditya Shankaracharya Mandir is a serene haven nestled amidst breathtaking natural beauty. From the moment you step onto the grounds, a sense of tranquility envelops you, making it a sanctuary for inner peace seekers. The temple's ambiance is simply mesmerizing, offering a serene escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life.

The peaceful environment is complemented by the symphony of birdsong, creating a harmonious atmosphere that rejuvenates the spirit. The meticulously landscaped surroundings enhance the temple's beauty, providing a serene backdrop for contemplation and meditation.

Visiting this sacred place instantly uplifts your mood, as the serene vibes and the spiritual energy intertwine seamlessly. Whether you're seeking solace, a quiet moment for introspection, or simply to admire the beauty of nature, this temple effortlessly caters to all.

The tranquil ambiance, coupled with the melodious tunes of nature, makes the Aditya Shankaracharya Mandir an absolute gem. A visit here promises not only a peaceful experience but also a connection to nature's serenity that lingers long after you've left. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a blissful retreat amidst stunning natural surroundings.

customer_updates.text: Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is really very peaceful and I loved sitting there in peace. Gurudwaras have always been a part of my routine. I feel more connected with God, and able to calm my mind of all the things that have veen worrying me. I would love to visit here again soon. featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is a place that truly radiates peace, devotion, and a strong sense of community. Located in Borivali, it offers a calm and spiritual escape from the fast-paced life of Mumbai.

The atmosphere inside the Gurudwara is incredibly serene, with soothing kirtans creating a deeply calming experience. Whether you visit regularly or for the first time, there’s a sense of warmth and welcome that makes you feel instantly at ease.

One of the most beautiful aspects is the langar seva, where everyone is served simple yet delicious food with humility and equality. The volunteers are kind and dedicated, ensuring everything is well-organized and that every visitor feels respected.

The premises are clean, well-maintained, and managed efficiently, allowing devotees to focus entirely on prayer and reflection. Overall, Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is not just a place of worship, but a space that offers peace, positivity, and a sense of belonging.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Bhoir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Attending my first Punjabi friend's wedding at a gurdwara was a beautiful experience. The entire atmosphere of the gurdwara, with its serene and welcoming ambiance, felt truly sacred and peaceful. As I entered, I was drawn to the calmness of the place, with the soft hum of prayers and the faint scent of incense filling the air. The sense of devotion was overwhelming yet calming, creating an indescribable sense of tranquility.

The wedding rituals themselves were simple yet deeply meaningful. The couple’s walk around the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture, symbolized their spiritual commitment. I was fascinated by the importance of equality and humility in the Sikh faith; everyone sat together on the floor, heads covered, symbolizing unity and respect. The langar (community meal) served after the ceremony was a highlight, as it embodies the Sikh value of selfless service.

The experience left a lasting impression on me. The gurdwara’s traditions and values, like community, compassion, and devotion, were truly inspiring. It felt like a place of pure spirituality and peace, and it made me appreciate the warmth and inclusivity of Sikh culture even more.

Our team provides Pure Veg Catering, and the layout makes food service very convenient. Guests always enjoy the meals and the overall vibe of the venue. Highly recommended for any event! For professional catering services, feel free to visit my profile." ~ chhaya caterers kandivali

featured_reviews.name: aruna mukerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn't even give one star but since i have to make others aware about the scammers here, i am doing so.

On the pretext of being a religious place, the representative of this Gurudwara functions hand-in-glove with valet parking organisations. On the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti, we visited in the evening and promptly handed over our car keys to the valet person. After more than 35 minutes of waiting, a threat to contact the police and a useless Gurudwara representative who did nothing, we were handed over our car without even an apology. Our car when we checked, had been running for 35 minutes and 10 kms with the AC running on 19 degrees. All this while, our old parents waited on the footpath while the valet guy chilled in our car and the Gurudwara representative was utterly useless and paid no attention to us or the urged the valets to do the right thing despite multiple requests.

It is such a shame that such a sacred place is associated with individuals who are focussed on scamming people. Next time, no matter what, don't hand over your car keys to any valet service here or any person from the Gurudwara.

I would also advice people to think twice before they even make any donations to this place, since this may just be the tip of the iceberg.

featured_reviews.name: Shwetali Shreya Ashok
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a very ancient shrine of Lord Shiva which is located in city Nallasopara which was the largest township on India's west coast and was known by different names Sopara, Soparaka, Shurparaka, etc.
The temple is off the main road and opposite the famous Chakreshwar lake.
It is a home to most impressive idol of Lord Brahma and some other ancient sculptures.
The Brahma idol here is a standing 'Sammukha' image, wearing a 'Jata-mukuta'. Of his three faces which are seen, the middle one only has a beard. The God holds the 'Akshamala' and the 'Sruva' in the lower and upper right hands, and the 'Kamandalu' and the 'Pothi' in the lower and upper left hands.
This is a relatively small temple and is noted as the holy place where Swami Samarth performed 'Dhyanam', 'Pratiṣhṭha' of a Ram Mandir near-by and blessed their 'Shishya' Swami Mayuranand who undertook a 'Sajiva Samadhi' here.
Next to samadhi, there is an open verandah which is again a small temple where two beautifully carved sculptures are embedded in the wall.
At a temple compound wall, there are lots of stone carvings of different Hindu deity. It is said that they were all retrieved from the Chakreshwar lake, The original temple was destroyed by Portuguese who destroyed most of the temples in Bassein(Vasai) area after they took the charge from the Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
The place is open on all days to visit.
Visiting Timings: 06:00 AM – 09:00 PM.

A wooden temple with fine details.

The real beauties are the 10th 11th century statues rescued from the nearby lake - the Chakreshwar talao.  These are kept in the compound for the public to appreciate, an inclusive cultural gesture.

Adjacent is another, more modern temple, housing yet more rescued sculptures.  Our guides were extremely knowledgeable about the provenance of these sculptures, which kept our group fully engaged.

The ruins of an older temple can be seen under a tarpaulin in the lane between the two temples.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Brahma Murti, Chakreshwar temple, Nalasopara, Mumbai, Maharashtra.

This Brahma idol was recovered from Chakreshwar talav and placed in the premises of Chakreshwar temple. As the idol is locked, I had to take pictures in parts.
This idol is three faced and the 4th face is missing.
Four faces of Brahma represents that bramha has created the world in all dimensions.
Beard (usually white) represents the maturity and experience required to create the universe.The idol in full form. Starting from the bottom left hand and going in clockwise direction, we can see Padma (Lotus) , Ledle (used mostly to serve offerings in Yajna), Book (mostly Vedas) and Kamandalam. You can see Swan which is the carrier of Brahma.

Also, you can see Ganas (association of people formed to attain the same aim, can also be called tribal people where God used to reside) in the same picture, near the legs of Brahma.You can see Toe Ring in his toe finger, which is also carved and Kadaa(an ornament) in both of his legs.

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Sakpal
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Ichhapurti Underground Ganpati Mandir in Wagholi is a remarkable spiritual site that offers a distinct departure from the typical temple experience. What makes it truly special is its unique location, situated 15 feet below the earth's surface. According to local history, the temple was constructed after a Swayambhu (self-manifested) idol of Lord Ganesha was discovered buried at this site. Rather than moving the idol to a traditional hilltop or ground-level structure, the devotees chose to build the temple downward, creating a subterranean sanctuary that feels sheltered from the outside world.
​Descending the stairs into the temple, visitors are immediately met with a noticeable drop in temperature and a profound sense of quiet. The interior is largely finished with warm wood paneling, which enhances the acoustics and creates an intimate, meditative environment. Because the sanctum is underground, the typical city noises of Nallasopara fade away, allowing for a focused and peaceful "Darshan." The idol itself, known as Ichhapurti (the fulfiller of desires), is beautifully adorned and serves as a powerful focal point for prayer and reflection.
​The temple is also conveniently located within a larger spiritual hub. Being part of the Fulare Charitable Trust complex, it sits right alongside the wooden-styled Swami Samarth Math and near the Wagheshwari Devi Temple. This proximity allows visitors to experience a complete "pilgrimage" within a single walking radius. Whether you are a devout follower or simply someone interested in unique architecture, the underground temple is a "must-visit" for its serene energy and the fascinating story behind its creation.

🙏😊"Icchapurti Ganpati Mandir – Where Wishes Truly Come True!"
Hidden beneath the ground in a peaceful corner of Wagholi, this small yet divine underground Ganpati Mandir is a true gem. As soon as you step inside, the sight of Lord Ganpati’s small and adorable idol fills your heart with calmness and devotion. It’s a place where your mind becomes still, and your prayers feel heard.

Many believe that any wish made here with a pure heart gets fulfilled, and honestly, it does feel magical. The vibe around Bappa is so positive, it’s like leaving all your worries at His feet. Each visit brings a sense of comfort and deep spiritual connection.

The best part? The journey itself. A peaceful bike ride through lush coconut trees, especially in the evening, is a whole experience in itself. The scenic views are breathtaking!

Right outside the temple, there’s a cute little garden with colorful flowers, where you can relax, take pictures, and kids can play too. And even during the monsoon season, this place looks like a beautiful painting — green, fresh, and full of peace.🙏🙏🙏🙏😊😊😊
